title: Why every AI story stars the same man 🗼

beats.big:
Ask AI
for a short
story.
beats.say: Ask an AI to write you a short story.
There's a good chance you'll meet Elias. The lighthouse keeper.

beats.sub: AI stories analyzed by Cornell researchers
beats.say: Cornell researchers had four big chatbots write twenty thousand stories.

beats.sub: stories built from the same 11 names and jobs
beats.say: The same eleven names and jobs showed up in eighty eight percent of them.
And Elias the lighthouse keeper starred in nearly two thirds.
He doesn't come from any famous book. Researchers couldn't trace him at all.

beats.sub: one theory: safety training narrowed the choices
beats.say: One theory: safety training steers AI away from risky stories, so it keeps landing on the safest guy in the room.
Try it yourself, and tell me in the comments who showed up.
Follow for more things the algorithm did.
